left.tested_scope: Crash-consistent OUTER evaluation state machine with durable intents, stable per-cell logical IDs, reconcile-before-execute, immutable outcomes, deterministic certification, and six real SIGKILL recovery boundaries in a SQLite-backed provider simulator.

right.tested_scope: Designed inherited-memory supersession experiment with a fixed verification budget of two records and a known critical provenance path. Native relevance-oriented allocation often misses that path and can preserve a withdrawn constraint; reallocating one of the same two verification slots to the provenance path sharply reduces the tested stale-memory error. The intervention is not a general scheduler and does not establish that all memory errors are caused by missed provenance verification; the held-out temporal inconsistency was separately corrected and replicated.

comparison.semantic_overlap: Both mechanisms try to prevent action from being governed by stale or ambiguous state by consulting a more authoritative record before proceeding, but they do so at different system layers and under different failure models.
distinguishing_scope: terminal_outer_sigkill_reference is an execution crash-consistency protocol: it journals intent, preserves stable logical IDs, reconciles uncertain prior effects after process death, freezes immutable outcomes, and certifies recovery across six SIGKILL boundaries. It does not test fixed-budget verification allocation over inherited memory or source supersession.

FE-354 is a memory-currentness experiment: under a fixed two-record verification budget it reallocates a check toward the provenance path of an inherited constraint to detect supersession. It does not specify durable execution intents, side-effect reconciliation, idempotent outcome handling, crash recovery, or certification.
